name: AI-001 - Audio Transcription Pipeline Worker
Description:
Implement a background queue worker that processes finished audio recordings and generates VTT transcripts. Expectation: Automated, accurate speech-to-text.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Worker pulls raw audio from Digital Ocean Spaces
- Transmits audio to Whisper API (or self-hosted transcription engine)
- Parses response into timestamped VTT/SRT format
- Saves transcript data to the database associated with the meeting ID

name: AI-002 - LLM Meeting Summarization & Chapter Extraction
Description:
Implement LLM prompt chain to generate meeting summaries and chapter markers from the raw transcript. Expectation: High-quality, readable meeting minutes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Pushes transcript text to GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet via API
- Prompt engineered to extract: Executive Summary, Decisions Made, and timestamped Chapters
- Sanitizes and stores the LLM output in the database
- Triggers 'Summary Ready' webhook to notify Kay's core backend

name: AI-003 - Automated Action Item Extraction
Description:
Enhance the LLM pipeline to identify action items and assignees from conversational text. Expectation: Smart task extraction from meetings.

Acceptance Criteria:
- LLM prompt specifically targets phrases like 'I will do X by tomorrow'
- Extracts Action Item string and maps it to a participant name if possible
- Saves Action Items as distinct relational rows in the database linked to the meeting
- Output format supports future integration with Jira/Trello via Kay's APIs

name: AI-004 - Independent AI QA Test Engine Setup
Description:
Initialize the automated QA test suite using Playwright. Expectation: A headless test suite capable of simulating full user journeys.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Playwright project configured with multiple browser contexts (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)
- Test suite structure created (Auth tests, Meeting Room tests, Host Dashboard tests)
- Can execute headless tests locally and generate HTML reports
- Mock media devices (fake camera/microphone feeds) configured for WebRTC testing

name: AI-005 - Core E2E Journey Tests (Login to Meeting End)
Description:
Write automated Playwright scripts testing the primary Konn3ct 'Happy Path'. Expectation: Verifies the most critical business flow.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Script logs in as Host, creates an instant meeting, and copies the join link
- Spawns a second browser context (Guest) joining via the link
- Asserts that both users appear in each other's participant lists
- Asserts that text chat messages are delivered successfully between contexts
- Asserts that ending the meeting successfully kicks the Guest

name: AI-006 - SLA Verification Checks (Performance QA)
Description:
Write QA scripts that measure actual performance metrics against Blueprint SLAs (Volume 7). Expectation: Ensures the app doesn't just work, but works fast.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Test measures time elapsed between clicking 'Join' and the video canvas rendering (Must be < 1.5s)
- Test measures API response times for authentication and meeting creation (Must be < 200ms)
- Fails the QA run if SLA thresholds are breached, even if the functional test passes

name: AI-007 - Support Ticket to Test Loop Integration
Description:
Create a standard template and process for converting bug reports into regression tests. Expectation: A bug never happens twice.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Documentation created for Support team on how to report reproducible steps to QA
- Script template for `regression.spec.ts` files
- CI/CD pipeline configured to run the `regression` test suite on every PR to ensure previously fixed bugs remain fixed
